business.body: The Company is engaged in the manufacturing, processing and marketing of premium woven fabrics and garments. Its product range spans synthetic and cotton shirting fabrics, bottom-weight fabrics, industrial fabrics and ready-made garments, sold to customers in domestic as well as international markets. Manufacturing is carried out at Umbergaon, Gujarat, on modern weaving and processing infrastructure able to produce fabrics in a variety of constructions, widths and finishes.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Woven fabrics:** Cotton shirting, Polyester-cotton blends, Cotton lycra, Cotton linen, Jacquards, Dobby fabrics, Printed fabrics, Structured fabrics, Blazer fabrics, Other fashion fabrics, Bottom-weight fabrics, Industrial fabrics
- **Garments:** Ready-made garments for the apparel segment

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Expand the product portfolio, with emphasis on value-added and premium fabrics (premium shirting, functional textiles, fashion fabrics and customised textile solutions).
- Strengthen customer relationships and improve customer service, retaining a customer-centric operating model.
- Increase operational efficiencies and enhance manufacturing capabilities through continued investment in modern machinery and technological upgradation.
- Expand market presence across both domestic and international/export markets.
- Maintain product innovation and continuous product development as the response to changing fashion trends and consumer preferences.
- Use the BSE SME listing (effective 03.12.2025) to strengthen the corporate profile, improve access to capital and accelerate future growth plans.
- Mitigate business risk through diversification across products and markets so no single product category or segment dominates.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report describes no named expansion project, no new plant and no dated commissioning or ramp-up plan. Manufacturing remains concentrated at the single facility at Umbergaon, Gujarat, equipped with modern weaving technology including Sulzer Projectile, Picanol, Rapier and Electronic Dobby looms; management states that continuous investment in modern machinery enables the Company to maintain high standards of quality and productivity, and that investments in modern machinery, product development and market expansion are expected to support sustainable long-term growth. Growth strategy is framed as enhancing manufacturing capabilities and operational efficiency rather than as a capacity addition with a timeline. The capital commitments note states that the estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on capital account and not provided for (net of advances) is Nil, with a Nil prior-year comparative, indicating no contracted capex outstanding at the balance-sheet date.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian textile industry remains one of the largest contributors to manufacturing output, exports and employment; management calls the outlook positive.
- Rising domestic consumption, favourable demographics and increasing disposable incomes are expected to support demand.
- Increasing preference for branded apparel, growth in organised retail and expansion of e-commerce platforms are cited as demand drivers.
- Government initiatives - PM MITRA Parks, the PLI Scheme, National Technical Textiles Mission and 'Make in India' - are expected to provide long-term growth opportunities for the sector.
- The 'China Plus One' sourcing strategy adopted by several global buyers is creating opportunities for Indian textile manufacturers to expand international presence.
- Demand for premium fabrics and value-added products is expected to grow steadily; increasing demand for premium shirting fabrics, functional textiles, fashion fabrics and customised textile solutions gives room to broaden the offering.
- Performance is influenced by domestic and global textile/apparel demand, consumer spending, raw material prices, fashion trends, export demand, foreign exchange movements and textile-sector government policy.
- Headwinds flagged: raw material price volatility, changing market dynamics, global economic uncertainties, competitive pressure on pricing/margins/market share from large integrated players, unorganised manufacturers and imports.
